topics.title: Introduction to React & Prerequisites
topics.keyConcept: React is a component-centric JavaScript library focused exclusively on rendering the View layer of single-page web applications using a Virtual DOM.
topics.content:
React is a declarative, efficient, and flexible open-source JavaScript library developed by Facebook for building user interfaces, specifically Single Page Applications (SPAs). It allows developers to create complex UIs from small, isolated pieces of code called 'components'. React is not a full MVC framework; it is purely focused on the **View layer** of the application.

Prerequisites: Before diving into React, developers must master modern JavaScript (ES6+):

  • Arrow Functions: Shorthand function syntax: const App = () => <div>Hello</div>;
  • Destructuring: Extracting properties: const { title, name } = props; or array destructuring: const [state, setState] = useState();
  • ES Modules: Code modularity using import React from 'react'; and export default MyComponent;

Real-World Project Example: Social media feeds (like Facebook or Instagram). The feed is a parent component containing multiple independent 'Post' components. Each post component contains 'LikeButton', 'CommentSection', and 'ShareButton' sub-components, allowing independent rendering when a user likes a post.
topics.commonMistakes: Describing React as a full-fledged MVC framework. Unlike Angular, React is a library. It does not include built-in routing, HTTP request clients, or state validation modules; these must be added using third-party libraries (React Router, Axios, etc.).
topics.interviewTip: When asked: 'What is React?', don't just say it is a framework. Emphasize that React is a **library** focused solely on the View layer of an application, utilizing a Virtual DOM to optimize rendering performance.

topics.title: Installation & Project Structure
topics.keyConcept: Modern React projects are built using Vite, scaffolded with standard files (package.json, index.html) and a main entry point that mounts to the DOM.
topics.content:
A modern React project is initialized using fast build tools like Vite rather than the legacy Create React App:

npm create vite@latest my-react-app -- --template react
cd my-react-app
npm install
npm run dev

Core File Structure:

  • package.json: Defines metadata, scripts (dev, build, lint), and dependencies (react, react-dom).
  • index.html: The HTML entry point. It contains a single mount point: <div id="root"></div> and a script tag importing src/main.jsx.
  • src/main.jsx: The bootstrap script. It uses ReactDOM.createRoot() to mount the React application inside the root div.
  • src/App.jsx: The main parent component.

Real-World Project Example: When a user navigates to a React SPA, the web server serves the static `index.html`. The browser then loads the bundled `main.jsx` script, which dynamically injects the entire interactive application layout into the `div id="root"` tag.
topics.commonMistakes: Trying to modify the DOM directly using `document.getElementById` inside React. React maintains a Virtual DOM; direct manual modifications bypass React's tracking, leading to rendering bugs and out-of-sync UI states.

topics.title: JSX: JavaScript XML rules and examples
topics.keyConcept: JSX is a syntax extension that compiles to standard React.createElement calls, enforcing self-closing tags and single parent root wrapping.
topics.content:
JSX is a syntax extension to JavaScript that looks similar to HTML. React uses JSX to describe what the UI should look like. JSX compiles down to standard JavaScript function calls: React.createElement(). For example:

// JSX Code:
const element = <h1 className="title">Hello World</h1>;

// Compiles to JavaScript:
const element = React.createElement('h1', { className: 'title' }, 'Hello World');

Strict Rules of JSX:

  1. Single Root: Components must return a single parent element. To group siblings without adding unnecessary wrapper divs, use React Fragments (<React.Fragment>...</React.Fragment> or the shorthand <>...</>).
  2. Close All Tags: All tags must be explicitly closed. Self-closing elements like image or line breaks must be written as <img /> or <br />.
  3. CamelCase Attributes: HTML attributes must use JavaScript naming conventions. Use className instead of class, and htmlFor instead of for.

Real-World Project Example: Building an input form. In JSX, you must write:

<>
  <label htmlFor="emailInput">Email:</label>
  <input type="email" id="emailInput" className="form-control" />
</>
topics.commonMistakes:
Attempting to return multiple sibling elements without a wrapping element. A component return statement like `return

Title

Text

;` will cause a compilation error. You must wrap them in `<>...`.
topics.interviewTip: If asked why React components must return a single root element, explain that a JavaScript function can only return a single value, and JSX compiles down to a single `React.createElement` function call.

topics.title: Variables & Comments in JSX
topics.keyConcept: JSX evaluates any valid JavaScript expression (variables, functions, maps) inside curly braces { }, and comments are written as {/* ... */}.
topics.content:
You can embed any valid JavaScript expression in JSX by wrapping it in curly braces { }. This includes variables, function calls, arithmetic operations, and arrays. Conditional rendering is done using JavaScript's ternary operator condition ? trueVal : falseVal or logical AND operator condition && element.

Code Example:

const user = { name: 'Aritra', role: 'Developer' };
const isLoggedIn = true;

const element = (
  <div>
    {/* Display welcome message conditional on login state */}
    {isLoggedIn ? <h1>Welcome back, {user.name}!</h1> : <h1>Please log in.</h1>}
    <p>Role: {user.role}</p>
  </div>
);

Comments in JSX: Standard JS comments (// or /* */) cannot be used inside JSX templates as they will be treated as plain text. You must wrap comments in curly braces: {/* This is a JSX comment */}.
topics.commonMistakes: Placing comments outside curly braces in JSX. Writing `// comment` inside a JSX div will literally display '// comment' on the user's web page.

topics.title: React Components & Lifecycle Phases
topics.keyConcept: Functional components use hooks to manage state, whereas legacy Class components use lifecycle methods. Component lifecycles have Mount, Update, and Unmount phases.
topics.content:
Components are reusable, independent blocks of UI. There are two types:

  • Functional Components: Simple JavaScript functions accepting `props` as arguments and returning JSX. Modern standard. They manage state using the useState Hook and side effects using useEffect.
  • Class Components (Legacy): ES6 classes extending React.Component, requiring a render() method and using this.state.

Component Lifecycle Diagram & Phases: Components go through three main lifecycle phases:

Lifecycle PhaseDescriptionClass Method EquivalentFunctional Equivalent (useEffect)
MountingComponent created and inserted into the DOMcomponentDidMount()useEffect(() => {}, []) (Empty dependency array)
UpdatingComponent re-rendered due to state/prop changescomponentDidUpdate()useEffect(() => {}, [dependency]) (Listens to dependencies)
UnmountingComponent removed from the DOMcomponentWillUnmount()useEffect(() => { return () => { /* cleanup */ } }) (Cleanup return function)

Real-World Project Example: Fetching profile details: A component mounts -> useEffect fires an API fetch call -> response returns and updates the local state -> component updates, rendering user details -> user logs out -> component unmounts, cleaning up timers.
topics.commonMistakes: Modifying state variables directly. Doing `state.count = count + 1` in functional components or `this.state.count = 5` in class components does not trigger a re-render. You must use `setCount(newVal)` or `this.setState({ count: 5 })`.
topics.interviewTip: Be prepared to explain the lifecycle phases. Mounting is for setting up (fetching data, starting timers), Updating is for responding to user inputs, and Unmounting is for cleanups (canceling network requests, removing event listeners).

practiceQuestions.question: What is React and what are its key features?
practiceQuestions.answer: React is an open-source JavaScript library developed by Facebook for building user interfaces. Its key features include: (1) Component-Based Architecture (reusable widgets), (2) Virtual DOM (optimized rendering), (3) Declarative UI, and (4) Unidirectional Data Flow.

practiceQuestions.question: What is JSX? Explain three strict syntax rules of JSX.
practiceQuestions.answer: JSX stands for JavaScript XML. It is a syntax extension for JavaScript that allows writing HTML-like code inside JS. Rules: (1) Every tag must be self-closing or closed explicitly. (2) It must return a single parent element (or a Fragment `<>...</>`). (3) HTML attributes must use camelCase conventions, such as `className` instead of `class` and `htmlFor` instead of `for`.

practiceQuestions.question: How do you embed variables and write comments inside a JSX block? Provide code snippets.
Differentiate between Functional Components and Class Components in React.
practiceQuestions.answer: Functional components are plain JavaScript functions that accept props and return JSX; they use Hooks to manage state and lifecycles. Class components are ES6 classes extending `React.Component`, require a `render()` method, and manage state/lifecycles via class methods (`this.state`, `componentDidMount`). Functional components are the modern standard.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the purpose of React Fragments?
practiceQuestions.answer: React components must return a single root element. When we want to group multiple sibling components without adding an extra wrapper node (like an unnecessary `<div>` that clutter the DOM and affects CSS flex/grid layouts), we wrap them in a React Fragment: `<React.Fragment>...</React.Fragment>` or the shorthand `<>...</>`.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is a key architectural feature of React?
mcqs.explanation: React uses a Virtual DOM which is a lightweight copy of the real DOM. When state changes, React updates the Virtual DOM first, runs a diffing algorithm, and updates the real DOM only where necessary.

mcqs.question: JSX gets compiled down to which standard JavaScript calls?
mcqs.explanation: Babel/Vite compiles JSX code into standard nested `React.createElement(type, props, ...children)` function calls.

mcqs.question: Which attribute must be used in JSX to define a CSS class?
mcqs.explanation: className must be used in JSX since class is a reserved keyword in JS.

mcqs.question: How do you write comments inside a JSX rendering block?
mcqs.explanation: Inside JSX templates, comments must be wrapped in curly braces and use JS multi-line comments: `{/* ... */}`.

mcqs.question: Which React hook is used to introduce local state variables in a functional component?
mcqs.explanation: useState is the core React Hook that lets functional components hold and modify component-local state.

mcqs.question: In React, what are 'props'?
options: Read-only properties passed from a parent component down to child components
States that can be modified by the component itself
mcqs.explanation: Props (short for properties) are inputs passed down from parent components to child components and are immutable inside the receiver.

mcqs.question: Class components require which method to return the component's JSX layout?
mcqs.explanation: All React Class components must implement a `render()` method that returns the JSX nodes describing the component UI.

mcqs.question: What is the shorthand syntax for React Fragments?
mcqs.explanation: Empty angle brackets `<>...</>` serve as the shorthand syntactic sugar for `<React.Fragment>...</React.Fragment>`.

mcqs.question: In a React project, what is the role of index.html?
options: It compiles the entire JavaScript code
It serves as the single page frame containing the target div where React mounts the component tree
mcqs.explanation:
React is an SPA library. index.html acts as the static shell containing a target container (usually `
`) where the JS engine mounts the virtual DOM.

mcqs.question: Which prerequisite JS concept is critical for importing other files and components in React?
mcqs.explanation: React applications are structured as modular files. We use ES6 `import Header from './Header'` and `export default App` to share components across files.
